citation: Montaser H, Patel KA, Balboa D, et al. Loss of MANF Causes Childhood-Onset Syndromic Diabetes Due to Increased Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress. Diabetes. 2021. doi:10.2337/db20-1174.
description: Documents human MANF loss of function and MANF knockout pancreatic endocrine cells with increased ER stress, supporting increased UPR genes after Manf perturbation.

citation: Yan Y, Rato C, Rohland L, Preissler S, Ron D. MANF antagonizes nucleotide exchange by the endoplasmic reticulum chaperone BiP. Nature Communications. 2019. doi:10.1038/s41467-019-08450-4.
description: Shows that MANF binds ER BiP and contributes to protein-folding homeostasis, providing a molecular bridge from MANF loss to ER chaperone stress.

citation: Liu XH, Zhang ZY, Andersson KB, et al. Cardiomyocyte-specific disruption of Serca2 in adult mice causes sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. Cell Calcium. 2010. doi:10.1016/j.ceca.2010.09.009.
description: Shows that loss of Serca2 in adult mouse cardiomyocytes induces GRP78, PERK/eIF2alpha signaling, CHOP, and apoptosis, supporting increased ER-stress markers after Atp2a2 perturbation.

citation: Jang I, Kim HB, Seo H, et al. O-GlcNAcylation of eIF2alpha regulates the phospho-eIF2alpha-mediated ER stress response. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta. 2015. doi:10.1016/j.bbamcr.2015.04.017.
description: Shows that O-GlcNAc modification of eIF2alpha modulates PERK/eIF2alpha/ATF4/CHOP signaling, supporting an indirect GFPT1/hexosamine connection to the ISR/ER-stress module.

citation: Ferrer CM, Lynch TP, Sodi VL, et al. O-GlcNAcylation regulates cancer metabolism and survival stress signaling via regulation of the HIF-1 pathway. Molecular Cell. 2014. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2014.04.026.
description: Reports that reducing O-GlcNAcylation activates ER stress and CHOP-linked apoptosis in cancer cells, providing pathway-level support for ER stress after perturbing hexosamine flux.

citation: Lee AS. The ER chaperone and signaling regulator GRP78/BiP as a monitor of endoplasmic reticulum stress. Methods. 2005. doi:10.1016/j.ymeth.2004.10.010.
description: Describes GRP78/BiP as a central ER chaperone that controls IRE1, PERK, and ATF6 activation, supporting a BiP-to-UPR bridge for Hspa5 perturbation.

citation: Kmiecik SW, Le Breton L, Mayer MP. Feedback regulation of heat shock factor 1 (Hsf1) activity by Hsp70-mediated trimer unzipping and dissociation from DNA. EMBO Journal. 2020. doi:10.15252/embj.2019104096.
description: Documents HSF1 as the metazoan transcription factor orchestrating heat-shock transcription, supporting decreased heat-shock chaperone genes after Hsf1 loss.

citation: Eberle D, Hegarty B, Bossard P, Ferre P, Foufelle F. SREBP transcription factors: master regulators of lipid homeostasis. Biochimie. 2004. doi:10.1016/j.biochi.2004.09.018.
description: Reviews SREBP isoform functions and the relative specificity of SREBP2 for cholesterol synthesis genes, supporting reduced sterol gene expression after Srebf2 loss.

citation: Porstmann T, Santos CR, Griffiths B, et al. SREBP activity is regulated by mTORC1 and contributes to Akt-dependent cell growth. Cell Metabolism. 2008. doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2008.07.007.
description: Shows that mTORC1 activity is required for Akt-dependent SREBP nuclear accumulation and SREBP target-gene induction, supporting sterol responses downstream of TSC/mTOR perturbations.

citation: Peterson TR, Sengupta SS, Harris TE, et al. mTOR complex 1 regulates lipin 1 localization to control the SREBP pathway. Cell. 2011. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2011.06.034.
description: Identifies an mTORC1-Lipin 1 mechanism controlling SREBP target genes and nuclear SREBP abundance, supporting a mechanistic chain from mTORC1 changes to lipid transcription.

citation: Kelsey I, Zbinden M, Byles V, Torrence M, Manning BD. mTORC1 suppresses PIM3 expression via miR-33 encoded by the SREBP loci. Scientific Reports. 2017. doi:10.1038/s41598-017-16398-y.
description: Uses loss of the TSC tumor suppressor complex as an mTORC1-activated state and links mTORC1 signaling to SREBP1/2 locus outputs, supporting Tsc1/Tsc2 sterol-module interpretation.

citation: Semizarov D, Kroeger P, Fesik S. siRNA-mediated gene silencing: a global genome view. Nucleic Acids Research. 2004. doi:10.1093/nar/gkh714.
description: Profiles RB1 siRNA knockdown and shows effects on E2F-linked cell-cycle, DNA-replication, and mitotic pathways, supporting the replication-gene response after Rb1 perturbation.

citation: Waaler J, Machon O, von Kries JP, et al. Novel synthetic antagonists of canonical Wnt signaling inhibit colorectal cancer cell growth. Cancer Research. 2011. doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-10-1282.
description: Shows that inhibition of canonical Wnt signaling at the destruction complex lowers AXIN2 and NKD1, supporting Wnt-target induction as the expected result of APC loss.

citation: Perobner I, Karow M, Jochum M, Neth P. LRP6 mediates Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and regulates adipogenic differentiation in human mesenchymal stem cells. International Journal of Biochemistry and Cell Biology. 2012. doi:10.1016/j.biocel.2012.07.025.
description: Demonstrates that LRP6 knockdown strongly decreases Wnt3a/beta-catenin reporter activity and that LRP6 rescue restores the pathway, supporting lower Axin2 after Lrp6 loss.

citation: Woo NS, Lu J, England R, et al. Hyperexcitability and epilepsy associated with disruption of the mouse neuronal-specific K-Cl cotransporter gene. Hippocampus. 2002. doi:10.1002/hipo.10014.
description: Shows that KCC2 disruption causes hippocampal hyperexcitability, seizures, and Fos up-regulation, directly supporting increased immediate-early genes after Slc12a5 loss.

citation: Lin WJ, Jiang C, Sadahiro M, et al. VGF and Its C-Terminal Peptide TLQP-62 Regulate Memory Formation in Hippocampus via a BDNF-TrkB-Dependent Mechanism. Journal of Neuroscience. 2015. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0584-15.2015.
description: Documents a VGF and BDNF/TrkB positive feedback loop in adult mouse hippocampus, giving a biologically specific but indirect bridge between Ntrk2 perturbation and Vgf RNA changes.

citation: Loregger A, Cook EC, Nelson JK, et al. A MARCH6 and IDOL E3 Ubiquitin Ligase Circuit Uncouples Cholesterol Synthesis from Lipoprotein Uptake in Hepatocytes. Molecular and Cellular Biology. 2015. doi:10.1128/MCB.00890-15.
description: Shows that loss of MARCH6 in hepatocytes increases SREBP-regulated cholesterol-biosynthesis genes, directly supporting increased sterol transcripts after Marchf6 perturbation.
